query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

falsification_experiment.design: Expose coated and uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples to air at 800-1000 °C for 5-10 hours and measure the oxidation rate and yield strength
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated sample shows no significant improvement in oxygen resistance and yield strength compared to the uncoated sample, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Paper card. Question: What are the individual effects of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr on the microstructure and mechanical properties (yield strength, ductility, and elevated-temperature performance) of equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr refractory high-entropy alloys?. System: Equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr and its five sub-alloys created by the subtraction method: HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi. Processing: Vacuum-arc melting of 99.9 wt.% (99.99 wt.% for Ti) pure elements stacked by melting point, re-melted at least four times, and solidified in a water-cool copper mold. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature, 800 °C, 1000 °C, 1200 °C, and 1400 °C; crosshead speed 0.36 mm/min (strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹); cylindrical samples 3.6 mm diameter x 6 mm height. Findings: HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy yield strength was 1512 MPa at room temperature and 556 MPa at 1200 °C.; HfMoTaTiZr (Nb removed) showed the highest room temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa

Question: Whether it is necessary to use all five elements (Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr) to achieve a random solid solution and good mechanical properties, or if reducing the system to 3 or 4 elements yields similar results.. System: HfNbTaTiZr system; specific alloys: HfNbTaTiZr (5-element), NbTaTiZr, NbTaTi, NbTiZr, TaTiZr, Nb0.5TaTiZr1.5, Nb1.5TaTiZr0.5 (3 and 4-element MEAs).. Processing: Vacuum arc melting in a water-cooled copper crucible; elements with 99.9% purity; ingots cast 8 times and flipped for mixing; no Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) or heat treatment applied to cast material.. Test conditions: Room temperature tensile testing with a strain rate of 2 × 10−4 s−1; Vickers hardness HV30 measurements; microstructure and phase analysis via SEM, WDS, and XRD..
